category: Turbobit Turbo-access storefront (reseller domain on the Turbobit platform)

free_tier.stated: Free mode (after a robot test and a time-out): about 5 Gb of downloads a day at a limited speed of about 55-60 KB/s, as written in the FAQ. The paid Turbo access plans are sold here.
free_tier.notes: The free path is on turbobit.net, not on this domain.

per_object_cap.stated: Premium account: 'Upload files up to 100 GB in size'; the cap for a free account is not published.
per_object_cap.notes: The 100 GB figure is described as transfer volume, not a single-object cap; unverified as a hard number.

retention.stated: not stated on the pages that rendered; Turbobit's own FAQ says files are kept while the account is active and longer for premium

egress.terms: Turbo plans on the premium page: 5 days 100 GB USD 5.95 (trial), 1 month 600 GB USD 9.95, 6 months 3600 GB USD 34.95, 1 year 7200 GB USD 59.95, 2 years 14400 GB USD 89.95; the daily and monthly caps are in limits.
egress.free_allowance: about 5 Gb a day in free mode at 55-60 KB/s

interface_detail: Single-page app (data-app="turbobit") whose tariff and checkout pages render entirely from JavaScript; the only readable surfaces are the marketing page and the FAQ.
tooling: Browser only. Support channels named on the FAQ: help2.turboget.net, online chat, and support by email, Skype and ICQ.
chaining: A second front door to the same Turbo codes sold by turbobitpremium.org and by the Russian forum resellers; useful only if its price or its payment rail differs, which could not be read.

limits.value: Premium: 25 GB per day and 600 GB per month (rules page); free mode: about 5 Gb per day (FAQ)

limits_note: The rules page also caps Premium at 250 files per day and at 10 different IP ranges per day; the Plus+ option doubles the volume limits to 50 GB per day and 1200 GB per month. Whether a datacenter address is accepted: not published.
binding_note: Premium downloads are capped at 25 GB per day and 600 GB per month on the rules page; the monthly volume is the plan size and is reached before any object cap applies.

identity_cost.detail: Registration needs a real email address, a password and agreement to the rules. A guest purchase needs an email address; payment methods listed are plastic cards, Skrill, cryptocurrency via Freekassa and resellers. No phone number or ID document is asked on the pages read.

reliability_note: The FAQ is a copy of Turbobit's own FAQ (it opens 'What is Turbobit.net?') and support runs on turbobit.net addresses, so a buyer is dealing with the Turbobit operator through a second domain. The FAQ and the rules page state different daily Premium download volumes.
confidence_note: The plans, prices, traffic volumes, free-mode volume, upload cap and registration inputs are quoted from the premium, rules and FAQ pages as read through a rendering reader; the plain HTML of /premium is an empty single-page-app shell.
